text:
olivia_sales: quick heads-up — Acadia Health wants a 2-week Private deploy POC. Primary asks: preserve client source IP to their onprem proxy, support mTLS from our connector to their egress proxy, and BYOIP mapping so their allowlist stays stable. also asking for delta pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity. can we confirm constraints before i reply?

mike_netops: ok — a few clarifying q's: 1) do they require PrivateLink (interface endpoint) only, or will we accept a transit/tgw + peering topology? 2) preserving src ip over privatelink typically needs their proxy to accept SNAT-preserved flows or we run egress on their side. If they insist on passthrough, we may need inline L4 proxy on their border.

mike_netops: fyi common approach i've used: terminate mTLS at customer proxy, have our connector keep client IP in X-Forwarded-For, and provide sticky EIP mapping for outbound so their ACLs can be simple. that means we control NAT mapping state — need to confirm failover semantics. :thinking:

jess_solutions: security Qs they'll push: KMS/HSM for keys, SOC2 + ISO attestation, data residency for logs, and network segmentation for admin plane. i can attach our 1-pager and compliance links. recommended we also offer a short firewall snippet for their netops. :thumbsup:

olivia_sales: perfect. mike — they'd prefer PrivateLink but said "open to architecture options if it preserves IPs". they called out port 443 only and a managed egress proxy IP range that must be stable during POC.

mike_netops: snippet for their firewall team:```allow tcp from 203.0.113.45/32 to 10.0.0.0/24 port 443  # our connector egress (BYOIP mapped EIP)
allow tcp from 198.51.100.0/28 to 10.0.0.0/24 port 443  # additional pool if we need burst
# keep-alive/tcp-timeouts: 30s idle before NAT translation refresh
```they should also open outbound to our control plane on 8443 if using Private deploy behind privatelink.

ryan_engineering: implementation notes: if PrivateLink can't preserve the original src IP through the customer proxy, fallback is to run an L4 passthrough on their edge (we can provide a lightweight appliance/container) or use our egress NAT with BYOIP + sticky session mapping. tradeoffs: passthrough = more customer infra work; NAT+BYOIP = simpler but we own mapping state and it's an extra cost (NAT gateway / elastic EIPs).

ryan_engineering: quick pricing guidance to feed back: Dedicated reserved GPU pool = predictable throughput pricing only; Private deploy = license + entitlements (support, compliance packaging) plus infra. for a 2-week POC i recommend quoting a short-term Private deploy eval credit + a not-to-exceed infra estimate. i'll draft numbers after i see their expected qps and model size.

olivia_sales: awesome. can we get: 1) final firewall snippet (jess + mike) 2) a 1-slide network diagram (ryan) that shows primary + fallback topologies, 3) a short compliance link + 1-pager (jess). aiming to reply to customer EOD tomorrow. i can join a quick sync if needed.

infra_bot: POC created: POC-ACADIA-1765432100 — owners: olivia_sales, jess_solutions, mike_netops; start: 2026-05-12; duration: 14 days.

jess_solutions: will assemble the compliance 1-pager and firewall snippet now, posting in this thread when done.

mike_netops: i'll sketch the exact privatelink vs transit rules and add notes about keepalive and session stickiness. expect a small config block in ~2h.

ryan_engineering: i'll draw the network diagram and include a short cost matrix (POC infra delta) — putting numbers as ranges until we get QPS.

olivia_sales: thanks team — i'll hold off replying to customer until we have the artifacts. ping me when ready and i'll schedule the sync. :pray:
